advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make heal_superseded_clone respect sync.pull=off (and the local-read context) the same way reads.ensure_fresh does, falling back to the existing refusal
evidence:
src/rebar/_store/freshness.py:297-298: `try:
        sync.reconverge(tracker)` with no sync-disabled guard
search for 'pull' in src/rebar/_store/sync.py returned no matches, so reconverge itself never checks the opt-out
src/rebar/_store/sync.py:305-309: reconverge always runs `_coordinated_fetch` before taking the lock
advisory.finding: heal_superseded_clone calls sync.reconverge without checking the `sync.pull = off` opt-out (or the local-read context) that the read-path reconverge honors. A write on a superseded clone now fetches and runs the stale-clone override, which discards unpushed events onto a backup ref, even when the operator disabled pulls. Before this change such a write was refused.
scenarios: An operator sets sync.pull=off to keep a clone pinned. Someone runs `git fetch`, which leaves a reclaimed baseline on origin/tickets. The next `rebar comment` fetches again and moves the clone onto the reclaimed history, discarding old unpushed events to refs/rebar/stale-override/.
advisory.suggested_fix: In heal_superseded_clone, resolve the code repo root and return early (leaving the retried precheck to refuse) when `reads._sync_disabled(root)` is true, or move that check into a shared helper used by both paths.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Give the superseded refusal its own message (store superseded by a reclaim; retry or run a sync) and surface why the heal failed instead of logging it only at DEBUG
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:441-448: `refusal = SupersededStoreRefused if stale.get("superseded") else CommandError` uses the same text for both: `recover with "rebar store fsck-recover" for stale rebase/merge dangling commits, or use "rebar store maintenance"`
src/rebar/_store/sync.py:274: `_reconverge(tracker, lock_timeout)`: reconverge drops the returned status (`lock-busy`, `fetch-failed`)

src/rebar/_store/freshness.py:300-301: `except Exception:
        logger.debug("superseded-clone heal failed; the write precheck decides", exc_info=True)`
advisory.finding: When the heal cannot move the clone (lock busy, fetch failed, override failed), its outcome is only logged at DEBUG, because reconverge discards _reconverge's status. The retried precheck then raises the generic DIVERGED message, which sends the user to `rebar store fsck-recover` / `rebar store maintenance` instead of saying the store was superseded by a reclaim and that a sync or retry would heal it.
scenarios: A busy MCP server holds the write lock past the heal's lock budget. The write is refused with advice to run fsck-recover or maintenance, which does not address a superseded store.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that disables or fails the heal on a superseded clone and asserts the write is refused, HEAD and the origin tip are unchanged, and only one retry happens
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:101: `except SupersededStoreRefused:` followed by `heal_superseded_clone(str(tracker))` and `return write()` (newly added retry; the second call's refusal is meant to propagate)
docs/concurrency.md:828-830 (added): "A clone the heal could not move (fetch failure, busy lock, failed override) is refused by the retried precheck"
src/rebar/_store/freshness.py heal_superseded_clone (added) swallows every exception from `sync.reconverge(tracker)`

Absence: none of the five tests in tests/interfaces/store/test_write_after_reclaim.py monkeypatches `heal_superseded_clone` / `sync.reconverge`, or asserts that a `SupersededStoreRefused` propagates on a superseded clone
The only evidence the read path was throttled is `_mark_recent_read`. No test shows that, with the heal disabled, the write on the superseded clone is refused.
advisory.finding: No test covers the documented path where the heal cannot move the clone. The retry wrapper should run the write exactly twice, let the second `SupersededStoreRefused` propagate, and commit nothing. No test checks this. Because of that gap, nothing in the suite shows the fixture reaches the new write-precheck heal at all. If the throttle pin stopped working, the read-path reconverge would heal the clone and all four positive tests would still pass without the fix.
scenarios: Named input: run `_supersede(tracker, origin, tmp_path)`, then monkeypatch `rebar._store.freshness.heal_superseded_clone` to a no-op, or make `sync.reconverge` raise, then call `rebar.comment(seed, ...)`. The expected outcome is a refusal (`SupersededStoreRefused` / RebarError with "ticket write refused"), HEAD and the remote tip unchanged, and the write attempted exactly twice. Nothing asserts any of this.
A regression that loops the retry, swallows the second refusal, or commits a local-only event after a failed heal would go undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_write_after_reclaim.py, add a test that runs `_supersede(...)`, then `monkeypatch.setattr(freshness, "heal_superseded_clone", spy)`, where the spy counts calls and does nothing. Then assert `pytest.raises(rebar.RebarError)` with "ticket write refused", `spy.calls == 1`, and HEAD/origin tip unchanged. This also proves the fixture reaches the write precheck rather than the read-path heal.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add unit tests asserting `write_blocking_divergence(...)["superseded"]` is True for a superseding lineage, and False for an unrelated lineage, a failed rev-parse, and a raising supersede probe
evidence: _remote_supersedes (added) returns False on a non-zero rev-parse and on any exception: `except Exception: ... return False`

tests/interfaces/store/test_write_after_reclaim.py test_write_against_an_unrelated_remote_is_still_refused asserts only `"ticket write refused" in str(exc.value)`, `"DIVERGED" in str(exc.value)`, HEAD unchanged and remote tip unchanged. The plain CommandError and the retried SupersededStoreRefused both produce that same message (src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:441-450).
tests/unit/test_gate_store_freshness.py:260-266 calls `write_blocking_divergence` but never checks the `superseded` key
advisory.finding: Nothing asserts the new `superseded` classification directly. The unrelated-remote test cannot tell `_remote_supersedes` returning False (the intended path: refuse with no heal) from it wrongly returning True (a pointless sync round, a failed override, then the same refusal). Both end with the same message and an unchanged HEAD and remote. The fail-closed branches (rev-parse failure, a probe exception) are also untested.
scenarios: Named input: the test's own `unrelated` record (`epoch_lineage: ["some-other-store-epoch"]`). If `_remote_supersedes` regressed to always return True, every test in the file would still pass.
Named input: a remote ref whose `rev-parse --verify <ref>^{commit}` fails, or a raising `compat.remote_epoch_supersedes_local`. The fail-closed False result is never asserted.
advisory.suggested_fix: In tests/unit/test_gate_store_freshness.py, build superseding and unrelated remote records, then assert `stale["superseded"] is True` / `is False`. Monkeypatch `compat.remote_epoch_supersedes_local` to raise and assert False. Alternatively, in the unrelated-remote interface test, spy on `freshness.heal_superseded_clone` and assert it was never called.
